related.note: Shermer takes Grusch's congressional testimony, that a witness told him about a spaceship, and explains it as a misidentified test drone. That is a different core claim about the same testimony.

plain: In 2023 a whistleblower named David Grusch gave sworn testimony before the US Congress about UFOs. In his own words, his claims rest on interviews with more than 40 witnesses over four years. A journalist, Michael Shellenberger, calls it really strong testimony. An official, Karl Nell, sums it up this way: Grusch told the House Committee on Oversight that a government program studies UFOs because they are real. A scientist, Donald Hoffman, describes the hearings more broadly. He says credible high-ranking military and other officials swore they had seen non-human biologics, meaning bodies or living material, and non-human technology, though he names none of them. If true, it would mean the US government knows of, and may hold, things not made by humans.
